_exemplar_note: ONE fully-built practice scenario to approve the card format before mass-extraction. Content OCR'd verbatim from AHA PALS 2025 Module 5, Appendix B, PDF pp.33-36. Prehospital lead-in used as default per OOH focus.
name: PALS Practice Case Scenario 3 — Lower Airway Obstruction (Child; Severely Ill)
source_ref: AHA PALS 2025 Instructor Manual, Module 5 Appendix B, pp.33-36 (PDF)

lead_in.prehospital: You are responding to a 911 call for a 10-year-old with breathing difficulty.
lead_in.ed: A 10-year-old girl is brought in by first responders from her home after her mother called 911 saying that her daughter had difficulty breathing.
lead_in.inpatient: You are called to the room of a 10-year-old girl who is being admitted from the emergency department for respiratory distress.
lead_in.picu: You are called to the room of a 10-year-old girl who is being admitted from the emergency department for respiratory distress.

card.overview: Emphasis is on rapid identification and management of respiratory distress / potential respiratory failure caused by lower airway obstruction (asthma). The provider must quickly recognize signs of distress (severe tachypnea and hypoxemia on room air) and provide initial therapy: 100% oxygen, nebulized albuterol, ipratropium, and oral corticosteroids. Continuous nebulized albuterol may be needed. Early expert consultation is indicated because this child has a history of status asthmaticus requiring multiple ICU admissions. The child improves, so acceleration of care is not required.
objectives: Recognizes signs and symptoms of respiratory distress caused by lower airway obstruction: increased respiratory rate and effort, prolonged expiratory time, and wheezing.
Performs correct initial interventions: oxygen, nebulized albuterol, ipratropium bromide, and corticosteroids.
Discusses importance of obtaining expert consultation if a child with asthma has a history of ICU admissions and/or fails to respond to initial interventions.

flow.identify: Immediate intervention needed — respiratory distress due to lower airway obstruction.
intervene: Activate the emergency response system / request additional assistance if needed.
Administer 100% oxygen by nonrebreathing face mask.

evaluate_primary_abcde.breathing: Moderate suprasternal and intercostal retractions; prolonged expiratory time; expiratory wheezes in the lower lobes; respiratory rate 40/min; SpO2 86% on room air (just before 100% oxygen).
evaluate_primary_abcde.circulation: Heart rate 140/min; pale skin; strong radial pulse; capillary refill 2 seconds; blood pressure 106/68 mmHg.

card.instructor_note: Child improves with initial therapy; acceleration of care is NOT required. History of status asthmaticus with multiple prior ICU admissions — drives the expert-consultation objective.
card.debrief_focus: Indications for positive-pressure ventilation; value of early expert consultation for asthma with prior ICU admissions.
card.ooh_grounding: Prehospital lead-in is the default. 'Expert consultation / ICU history' is grounded for OOH as medical-direction / receiving-facility consult; no ER-specific reframe needed since the card ships a native prehospital scene.
